web.title: Geeli Mehendi Challenge: Shaadi Kitty Party Game Rules
web.description: Geeli Mehendi is a funny shaadi season kitty party game: wear socks on your hands like wet mehendi and finish 3 small tasks in 1 minute. Rules, steps, FAQ.
web.intro: Geeli Mehendi is a one minute kitty party game where every lady wears a pair of socks on her hands, pretending her mehendi is still wet, and must unwrap and eat a toffee, fix a hair clip on her dupatta and cross 3 numbers on a Housie ticket. The first lady to finish all three tasks wins the round. The crazy twist: whenever the host shouts "Mehendi kharab!" everyone must freeze with palms up for 5 seconds, and anyone who touches anything starts all the tasks again. It needs only socks, toffees, hair clips and old Housie tickets, so it is perfect for a shaadi season or mehendi theme kitty.
materials: One pair of socks per player (thick woollen socks make it harder and funnier)
One big hair clip (claw clip or banana clip) per player
An old Housie or Tambola ticket and a pen per player
A phone timer set to 1 minute
steps: Play in rounds of 4 ladies. Each one sits with a toffee, a hair clip, a Housie ticket and a pen in front of her.
Everyone pulls a sock over each hand, like gloves over wet mehendi. Fingers must stay inside the socks the whole time.
The host starts a 1 minute timer. Task 1: unwrap the toffee with sock hands and eat it.
Task 2: open the hair clip and fix it on your own dupatta or kurta so it stays without falling.
Task 3: pick up the pen and cross out any 3 numbers on the Housie ticket.
At any moment the host may shout "Mehendi kharab!": everyone freezes with palms facing up for 5 seconds, and anyone who touches anything during the freeze starts the tasks again.
The first lady to finish all three tasks raises her hands and wins the round. Round winners play a final.
rules: Fingers must stay inside the socks. If a finger comes out, that task must be done again.
During the "Mehendi kharab!" freeze, anyone who touches anything starts all three tasks from the beginning.
A dropped toffee must be picked up and eaten before the task counts, so nothing is wasted.
The first lady to complete all three tasks in order wins; if nobody finishes in 1 minute, the one with the most tasks done wins.
variations: In the final, round winners wear rubber kitchen gloves over the socks.
Tie one hand behind the back so only one 'mehendi hand' can be used.
Play in pairs: one lady is blindfolded and does the tasks while her partner only guides with words.
tips: Thick woollen winter socks make the game slower and much funnier.
Use big claw or banana clips; small bobby pins are too hard and fiddly.
Keep the freeze call random, once or twice per round, to catch people mid task.
Ask the ladies who are waiting to record the round on their phones; the reactions are the best part.

faq.q: How many players do you need for Geeli Mehendi?
faq.a: It works for 8 to 20 ladies played in rounds of 4. Round winners then play a final to find the champion.

faq.q: What do you need to play the Geeli Mehendi game?
faq.a: A pair of socks, a toffee, a big hair clip, an old Housie ticket and a pen for each player, plus a phone timer.

faq.q: How do you win the Geeli Mehendi challenge?
faq.a: Be the first to unwrap and eat the toffee, fix the clip on your dupatta and cross 3 Housie numbers, without your fingers leaving the socks.

faq.q: Is Geeli Mehendi good for a shaadi or mehendi theme kitty party?
faq.a: Yes. The whole game is built around the feeling of wet mehendi on your hands, so it fits mehendi functions, sangeet nights and wedding theme kitties.

faq.q: How long does the Geeli Mehendi game take?
faq.a: Each round is 1 minute, so with 8 to 20 ladies the whole game including a final takes about 10 to 15 minutes.
